content:
Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year is rumored to revolve around two models: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Ultra. Here are the three biggest feature differences—not including price—that could influence your upgrade decision.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but worth mentioning because it's also the most significant.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic form factor that iPhones have used for years. The screen size and overall design are reportedly identical to the previous generation. If you want the traditional iPhone feel, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top pick.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable model. With a completely different form factor, the outer screen is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner screen resembles an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Still Reigns Supreme

Apple has consistently equipped its Pro models with the most advanced and innovative camera technology, and this year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to offer the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: no telephoto lens.

Rumors suggest you'll still get the same main lens, ultrawide lens, and front-facing camera on the iPhone Ultra as those on the Pro lineup. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro series, and is expected to deliver even better performance this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, but with Different Materials

Both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are expected to use the same A20 Pro chip. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance may vary slightly.

The iPhone 18 Pro will continue the unibody aluminum design introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, also featuring a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance better than its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures during demanding tasks.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will adopt a minimalist titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though only one leaker has mentioned this so far. However, due to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may perform slightly worse in direct sunlight or during intensive tasks.
